label: Turing's condition for diffusion-driven instability (two species, linear)
statement_en: For the linearisation of a two-species reaction-diffusion system at a uniform steady state that is stable without diffusion (trace of J negative, determinant positive), some spatial mode q > 0 is linearly unstable if and only if 2*sqrt(Du*Dv*det J) < Dv*a + Du*d. Corollary: with equal diffusivities no mode is unstable (two species only).

hypotheses.name: Delphi.Turing.WellMixedStable
hypotheses.statement: The uniform steady state is stable without diffusion: a + d < 0 and a*d - b*c > 0 for the reaction Jacobian ![![a,b],![c,d]].
hypotheses.source: Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37-72, doi:10.1098/rstb.1952.0012 (resolved via Crossref 2026-11-02); claim notation of turing-ddi in claim-sources/math-bio-claims/claims/key-claims.json

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: two species, smooth kinetics linearised about a homogeneous steady state, constant positive diffusivities, unbounded domain (all real q admissible), no growth or mechanics. The equal-diffusivity corollary is two-species only: with three or more species Turing instability with equal diffusivities is possible (Marcon et al. 2016, doi:10.7554/eLife.14022).

evidence.note: A proof that the condition follows from the linearised model; it says nothing about whether any tissue is such a system. The claim's instantiation in organisms is the turing-1952-* instance claims and turing-morphogen-hypothesis.
